data.body:
ADR SOURCE MATERIAL FOR S9 — PART 1/4: DECISIONS Gathered 2026-08-03 by a read-only research pass over all 40 epic descendants plus 7b22, ed82, a574 (which are NOT in list-descendants — they are detached; see Part 4). Code citations were opened and line-verified at HEAD 6c390d7a0a. Raw ticket dumps: /tmp/adrsrc/*.txt, notes /tmp/agent{A,D,E,F}.md. READ PART 4 FIRST IF YOU ARE WRITING THE ADR: two of this ticket's own premises are FALSE.

## THE SEAM
D1 The seam is pydantic-ai's `provider_factory` hook, not a rebar invention. 7468: "Upstream directs
   user-configurable-provider apps to exactly this hook (pydantic-ai#1343) rather than patching
   `infer_provider`, so rebar depends on a supported contract." providers.py:132-176; sole call site
   runner.py:350.
D2 It is a per-run SESSION object, not a bare function, because of client teardown: "The hook's return
   type carries a `Provider` only, with no channel for the retrying httpx.AsyncClient." One session per
   run(), never shared, so `_closeables` needs no locking. providers.py:74, :102, :309-321, :323-327.
D3 S1 landed as a PURE RELOCATION before any new provider used it, so Bedrock/OpenAI were additive
   registrations rather than surgery on run().
D4 Builder BODIES live in leaf modules; the REGISTRY and every call site live in providers.py.
   Registry providers.py:106-109; openai registered conditionally :117-118, :163-164. Bodies
   anthropic_model.py:160, bedrock_model.py:88, providers.py:256-290.

## CAPABILITIES
D5 Capability decisions read ModelProfile, NEVER a provider-name string. capabilities.py:1;
   structured.py:43-60 branches on caps.native_structured_output at :58; cache_settings_for dispatches
   solely on caps.prompt_cache_style. `_NATIVE_OUTPUT_PROVIDERS` is GONE (grep: zero hits).
D6 prompt_cache_style is derived from profile FIELD PRESENCE, not concrete type — a hard constraint.
   f184: "the attested v6 plan said prompt_cache_style is derived from the profile's CONCRETE TYPE
   (isinstance BedrockModelProfile). That is unimplementable in CI. BedrockModelProfile is exported only
   from pydantic_ai.models.bedrock, which imports botocore at module top; there is no SDK-free
   pydantic_ai.profiles.bedrock; and boto3 appears in pyproject.toml ONLY under the reviewbot extra. An
   isinstance check would break the stdlib-only `import rebar.llm` contract AND fail CI."
   capabilities.py:209-248.
D7 TWO override tables, deliberately apart, both membership-keyed. `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` is an ORDERED
   TUPLE of (predicate, overrides), "deliberately NOT a dict keyed by provider name, for two reasons: a
   name key would reintroduce exactly the string matching this story exists to remove, and it could not
   express the single rule below, which must span two different HOSTS of the same model family."
   capabilities.py:138-153. `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` keys on the exact full model id,
   :186-206. 2932 on why separate: "f184's keys on capability shape (what kind of model is this), this
   one keys on a specific model's API defect (this exact id rejects a parameter)." And why f184 was not
   widened: "f184 is closed and its plan-review attestation is signed... widening that signature would
   silently redefine a shipped, signed contract from a downstream leaf. The rule is that the parent wins."
D8 `_is_claude` keys on bedrock_thinking_variant == "anthropic"; BOTH arms required. f184:
   "Bedrock-hosted Claude's profile is a BedrockModelProfile, NOT an AnthropicModelProfile (verified —
   sibling subclasses), so an isinstance(AnthropicModelProfile) test alone would miss the very models this
   epic exists to support." And: "this is a capability FIELD READ whose value happens to be a string enum
   — materially different from resolved.startswith('anthropic')."
D9 supports_thinking goes on the record NOW, before anything signs it, though nothing branches on it:
   "the signed record must already state whether the model that produced each historical verdict was
   CAPABLE of thinking, because that fact cannot be reconstructed later... Adding the field after S5 ships
   is also strictly more expensive." Labelled "a deliberate, documented exception to 'no field without a
   consumer'." Same argument reused for supports_temperature on 343b.

## THE REGISTRY-MEMBERSHIP QUALIFIER
D10 Qualification by REGISTRY MEMBERSHIP, matching OSS consensus. 7b22: "The shape test works for the ids
   we have, but it answers the wrong question. It asks 'does this prefix LOOK like a provider name?' when
   the answer needed is 'IS this prefix a provider name?'" Consensus: LangChain's
   `model.split(":",1)[0] in _BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`, LiteLLM's `provider_list`, pydantic-ai's
   `infer_provider_class` raising. Code config.py:214-241 (KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES), decider :244-261.
D11 The set is a LITERAL of plain strings — no imports, no lazy loading: "split_provider_qualifier runs
   during config resolution, where the optional [agents] extra may not be importable at all."
D12 NO name is grandfathered; neither `test` nor `google_genai` is a member. Deciding probe against
   pinned pydantic-ai 1.107.1: infer_model("test:foo") -> ValueError: Unknown provider: test;
   infer_model("google_genai:gemini-2.0") -> Unknown provider: google_genai. "Granting either name
   membership would make rebar MORE permissive than the library it wraps, which is backwards."
D13 Two paths, deliberately ASYMMETRIC: strict on a CONFIGURED provider, permissive on an unrecognized
   INLINE prefix — because "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0".partition(":") yields a prefix that
   is by construction not a provider name. "Falling back to 'not qualified' is the only answer that keeps
   a colon-bearing model id intact." Configured-provider validation model_classes.py:247-252.
D14 GUARD ORDER is the real fix, and NEVER silently fall back. 03b0: "an explicitly configured provider is
   checked FIRST, before the model string is scanned at all." Policy verbatim: "GRACEFUL FALLBACK IS THE
   WRONG CHOICE HERE... its origin was 41 of 42 calls silently reaching direct Anthropic... Fail closed
   (already) + fail fast (to add); never fall back."
D15 `:` stays the separator. "pydantic-ai's own KnownModelName contains TWO-COLON entries
   ('bedrock:anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0')... no project was found regretting a separator."
   Direction of travel worth an ADR line: "pydantic-ai REMOVED bare-name inference in v2.0.0b1."

## NATIVE BEDROCK
D16 Native BedrockConverseModel + BedrockProvider, ambient AWS credential chain, NO rebar-managed key.
   bedrock_model.py:41-88; config.py:450-453 records there is deliberately no Bedrock credential field.
D17 Documented default `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` — an INFERENCE-PROFILE id, because on-demand ids
   are not invokable, and it is the MEASURED-caching id. bedrock_model.py:38, ValidationException :17-20.
D18 Bedrock sets exactly TWO cache breakpoints for parity, not three: "An earlier draft named a third
   (bedrock_cache_messages); that is REJECTED for parity... Enabling message caching on Bedrock alone
   would make it cache MORE than Anthropic." LATER SUPERSEDED ON BOTH ARMS BY dd27 — see D25.
D19 temperature is carried as a CAPABILITY via a second exact-id table: "_REBAR_OVERRIDES predicates
   receive only the ModelProfile, and BedrockModelProfile carries NO per-model identifier, so the only
   predicate expressible would strip temperature from us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 too — the
   measured-good default." On the apparent relapse: "This is model-id matching, and that is deliberate,
   not a relapse... recording a known per-model API defect is a different thing, and it is what
   pydantic-ai itself does." DENYLIST over allowlist: "an unknown-but-affected model then fails LOUDLY,
   whereas an allowlist would silently drop temperature from an unknown-but-fine model."
D20 Error-CONTENT-keyed translation in failure.py, never a provider branch. Three-conjunct predicate
   (400-or-ValidationException AND a sampling-param name AND a rejection word) "so an unrelated 400 is
   NOT swallowed."
D21 The Bedrock region pre-check raises a typed LLMConfigError rather than inventing a default.
   bedrock_model.py:67-88.

## TIERS AND VERDICT PROVENANCE
D22 ADDITIVE sibling `provider_provenance` object; the `model` string is untouched. "Additive-only is
   deliberate: it makes this a backward-compatible payload change, so an older reader ignores the new key
   and no store-compatibility gate or migration is required." capabilities.py:395-446; stamped
   runner.py:405-407; persisted completion_sidecar.py:213/:231, plan_review/sidecar.py:637,
   code_review/sidecar.py:106.
D23 SIGN ON EVERY TIER; give the consumer a lever instead of a refusal: "a contributor running Ollama can
   still exercise the gates, which matters for the OSS on-ramp."
D24 REUSE the capability record, never recompute; `.hostname` never `.netloc`; OMIT the key where no model
   ran. "Provenance must stamp THAT record, not call capabilities_for again — a second resolution can
   silently diverge from the record that actually drove the run." Guard
   test_verdict_provenance.py:115. Credential trap named: "runner.py:650 uses parsed.netloc, which
   RETAINS user:secret@." Omission: "A cfg-derived record at a site where nothing ran would reproduce the
   EXACT defect this record exists to fix."

## PROMPT CACHING
D25 A THIRD breakpoint on the AGENTIC path only, with DIFFERENT keys per arm (anthropic_cache=True /
   bedrock_cache_messages=True). capabilities.py:454, :503-514. "System-only is the documented minimum for
   a STATIC-PROMPT workload; it is not the shape for an agent." Budget: pydantic-ai's
   _limit_cache_points sets MAX_CACHE_POINTS = 3 if automatic_caching else 4; this puts rebar at 3.
D26 Per-model cache floor from Anthropic's PUBLISHED table; empirical brackets are VERIFICATION ONLY.
   e3cd: "Anthropic's PUBLISHED table, not the brackets: platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/
   prompt-caching, section 'Minimum cacheable prompt length', read 2026-08-02. The ticket's two
   independent measurements were used only to VERIFY it, and all three agree." 13 entries at
   512/1024/2048/4096, capabilities.py:68-84. Rejected: a single global — "The published table is NOT
   monotonic across generations, which is exactly why one global could not express it."
   THIS IS THE GOLD STANDARD FOR CITATION HYGIENE IN THIS EPIC — published URL + read date, brackets
   explicitly demoted.
D27 Bedrock ids are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the floor table: "Anthropic's table states these minimums
   apply on every platform EXCEPT Amazon Bedrock, which publishes its own. rebar has measured none of
   Bedrock's, so a Bedrock model falls through rather than being assigned a guessed number."
D28 Compare the MARKED PREFIX, not total input_tokens; and DO NOT add the floor to the signed record:
   "Adding a 5th key to its capabilities record would change the bytes of already-signed gate verdicts;
   the floor is a published property of the model, recoverable from the recorded model id."

## MODEL CLASSES AND PER-PASS CONFIG
D29 THREE capability classes are the universal interface; internals never name a model id. "Each class is
   a config SLOT the operator fills... The three names are SLOTS the client fills, not presets rebar
   ships." Root cause: "one knob for four passes. REBAR_LLM_MODEL is a single scalar, and a scalar cannot
   express a per-tier mapping." NOTE: no argument for the number THREE exists anywhere — see Part 4.
D30 KEYSTONE: class names are RESERVED VALUES in the existing model-string space — no schema change.
   "the DSL stays closed and its VALUE space gains three reserved words." model_classes.py:309-332.
D31 CORRECTION TO D30: there is NO single funnel — one FUNCTION, three CALL SITES. eb58 verbatim:
   "CORRECTION to the keystone decision — my 'ONE funnel' claim was WRONG... I proposed the exact cycle I
   had just prohibited." And: "What I gave up is the false claim that a single interception point exists.
   Pretending it did would have shipped a change where the step path resolved classes correctly and its
   tests passed, while ladders and verifiers silently passed the literal strings 'standard'/'frontier'
   through to a provider as if they were model ids."
D32 Secrets stay ENV-ONLY, deliberately diverging from LiteLLM: "LiteLLM puts api_key inline in
   litellm_params and rebar must not copy that." Enforced model_classes.py:80-83.
D33 Layering: tables merge recursively (leaf key wins); ARRAYS ARE REPLACED WHOLESALE. "a table-level
   replace would force CI to restate an entire class slot to change one field, which IS the duplication
   this pointer exists to avoid." And: "Appending is rejected because a chain that can only grow can never
   be shortened, reordered, or cleared by an environment." Precedence: CLI -c > env >
   REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE > discovered config file > built-in default.
D34 The env-var names are string LITERALS, not f-strings, each read through its own literal
   os.environ.get, because scripts/gen_env_registry.py statically scans for literal arguments — a
   formatted name would silently escape the documented registry. model_classes.py:99-104, nine names
   :105-115.
D35 Per-step class assignments stated EXACTLY so no executor guesses; batch steps use a SINGLE-RUNG
   model_ladder. base->frontier; round_a/round_b->model_ladder:[frontier]; verify->standard;
   coach->standard. "A review round blocked twice on this being unspecified." Why not a step-level
   `model:` on a batch step: "A step-level model: on a batch: step is a SILENT NO-OP... Because model IS
   a legal step key, such a declaration VALIDATES and is then discarded — and a test asserting only that
   the YAML carries a class token would PASS while runtime behaviour was unchanged. An earlier version of
   this very table made that mistake." Why ONE rung: "A ladder escalates per criterion, so the model that
   actually answers a given criterion is NOT determinate."
D36 REBAR_LLM_MODEL is DEPRECATED with a migration window, not a permanent alias: "There are few clients
   today and a single-scalar knob alongside a class model is precisely the ambiguity this work removes."
   During the window it fans out to all three classes (docs/llm-framework.md:155-157).
D37 STANDING OPERATOR RULE (afeb): "For REVIEWS, Pass-2 and Pass-4 are DESIGNED to use a sonnet-equivalent
   model (the standard class), with LIMITED ESCAPE HATCHES for escalation to a higher class (frontier)."
   And: "the fix is NOT 'give these calls frontier' — the default for verification/judging work is
   standard. A site that needs frontier must justify it as an explicit, bounded escape hatch."
D38 RESTORATION (77ed): Pass-1 finder on frontier/opus; Pass-2 verify and Pass-4 coach on standard/sonnet.
   "That split is what _verifier_cfg was written to express, and its own docstring already asserts it...
   The docstring has simply been false since 2026-06-27. This is a RESTORATION, not a new preference."
D39 Single-call ops keep cfg.model; the class vocabulary exists for MULTI-pass gates. "rebar review is a
   SINGLE call: there is no 'here versus there' to differentiate." Cost of getting it wrong: "an operator
   who steers by setting the bare llm.model CONFIG-FILE key no longer steers rebar review at all."
D40 `self._config` is the FLOOR; `req.config` is the per-call OVERRIDE. THE EPIC'S SINGLE ROOT
   ARCHITECTURAL DEFECT was one line: runner.py:239 `cfg = self._config`. Shape decision: "Substitute into
   a COPY of the config, not a loose variable at the resolution point... Reading a separate model variable
   at _pai_model only would have left the provider session built for the FLOOR's provider."
D41 Escalation TARGETS move to the class vocabulary; escalation WINDOWS stay keyed on concrete model
   families. Provider-agreement rule: "providers differ on a HIGHER rung -> drop the rung... there is no
   honest target. Escalation stops and the existing too-big failure finding reports it — a visible outcome
   instead of a silent provider jump."
D42 Fix the CONSUMPTION of MODEL_LADDER, not the table. 1157: "Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 genuinely share a
   1M window. The table is honest; the ladder's USE of it is not." 48b3: "The two error directions are not
   symmetric. Under-blocking is silent: the review proceeds and truncates. Over-blocking is loud and
   actionable." Hence an unlocated window resolves to the ladder MINIMUM, and an unlocated primary to
   [model] not [] — "Returning [] would discard the single-criterion retry, which is the step that most
   often succeeds."

## BEST-EFFORT OPENAI-COMPATIBLE
D43 base_url is provider CONFIGURATION, not provider SELECTION. D44 The openai builder is registered ONLY when cfg.base_url is set, and the reason does not rest on SDK
   absence: "with no base_url configured, rebar has NOTHING TO CONTRIBUTE to provider construction — no
   endpoint to inject, no key to place, no profile to override... rebar builds a provider only when it has
   configuration to apply." providers.py:110-118.
D45 The profile override rides the PROVIDER, not a model argument — forced by the seam: "rebar's factory
   hands back a Provider and pydantic-ai's infer_model constructs the model itself — so a model-level
   argument is unreachable from the seam." Justification: "the OpenAI profile describes OpenAI's HOSTED
   API. A custom base_url is by definition a different server... Withdrawing that one flag makes the
   plan's original claim true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by assumption."
D46 _pai_check_config VALIDATES instead of refusing. structured_run.py:576-597. Two remaining errors:
   api_key without base_url (:583-588), non-absolute base_url (:589-597).
D47 The optional SDKs are added to the `dev` extra ONLY, so CI can prove the story. Precedent: "dev
   already installs mcp, which is likewise an OPTIONAL runtime extra."

## STANDING OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED ON THE EPIC ITSELF
OD1 Keep stacking; ignore LOC-only Verified -1s; keep the TOP clean; operator manually overrides ancestors
   to submit. "Gerrit submitted_together confirms all 10 are one submit set with 5 submittable=False, so
   that override is genuinely required." Feature-branch verdict: "A feature branch was tried and DOES NOT
   HELP: submit requirements are inherited project-wide and CI fires on feature-branch changes, so it is
   strictly more review, not less. That branch has been deleted."
OD2 The per-FUNCTION length ratchet is REJECTED FOR NOW; SUPERSEDES ADR 0056's standing recommendation.
   MEASURED across 3,292 functions under src/rebar: 21 over 200 lines, 38 over 150, 62 over 120, 101 over
   100, ten worst spanning six subsystems. "Adopting it would either break the build in six subsystems at
   once or require an allowlist — and epic 716f deliberately DRAINED AND REMOVED the module-size
   allowlist." Consequence: "the module-level reworks are no longer a belt-and-braces mitigation — THEY
   ARE THE ONLY DEFENCE... the SEAM TEST becomes the substitute ratchet, and is now load-bearing."
OD3 Two orphaned open tickets (3768, 5e75) parented into the epic; "For 5e75 it is a REAL scope change."
   Load-bearing sequencing rule: "a ticket's PARENT is part of its material fingerprint... Parent before
   reviewing, never after."
OD4 THE BIG ONE — cross-model verdict comparison is OUT OF SCOPE. Operator ruling verbatim: "LLMs are
   non-deterministic. Expecting two runs to produce identical results is unrealistic AND BEYOND THE SCOPE
   OF THIS EPIC. The epic's scope is to ensure THE SAME PAYLOADS REACH THE LLM and THE LLM HAS THE SAME
   TOOLS AVAILABLE, regardless of model and provider. COMPARING MODELS AGAINST ONE ANOTHER IS OUT OF
   SCOPE." Best sentence for a "why the bar changed" section: "My earlier judgement — that the ticket
   could not honestly close as 'Bedrock cleared the bar' — was correct under the OLD criteria; the … [truncated by reconciler]
